ultrathink do an analysis here what we need to get the full loop in our skills to start improving the
   complete flow Two Loops You Need to Know
  Peter Skøtt Pedersen
  Peter Skøtt Pedersen
  People - AI - Software


  April 8, 2026
  If you want to improve agent output over time, you need to run two loops not one.

  The inner loop happens during a running session. The agent detects a problem, checks its work, and
  tries to recover without you touching anything.

  The outer loop happens across sessions. You capture where the agent failed, figure out what knowledge
   was missing, and encode it somewhere the agent can reach next time.

  Both loops are required. The inner loop catches failures in the moment. The outer loop ensures the
  same failures stop happening. Without both, you are not improving the system, you are just managing
  it.

  A compact way to think about it:

  Inner loop: detect, verify, recover
  Outer loop: inspect, encode, regress-test

  Thorsten Ball has a useful framing for why agents fail in the first place: the knowledge required to
  complete a task has to live somewhere. It usually lives in one of three places:

  Your prompt/spec. What you explicitly tell the agent.
  The codebase or harness. Types, tests, tools, conventions, documentation anything the agent can read
  and reason from.
  Training data. What the model already knows from the world.

  If the knowledge exists in at least one of those places, the agent usually has a path forward. If it
  doesn't exist in any of them, there's a gap. The agent will plough through anyway and fill the gap
  with something: infer, improvise, guess. Sometimes that works. Often it doesn't.

  In workflows, the failure is often not the model. It's the assumption that the knowledge was
  somewhere it wasn't.

  This gets more dangerous as you move to end-to-end autonomous workflows. One gap mid-run and the
  whole thing goes sideways, silently. You can catch some of this with CI pipelines or quality gates,
  and you should. But gates only cover what you thought to test for. The gaps that slip through are the
   ones nobody anticipated.

  The two loops are how you close those gaps systematically, over time.

  The Inner Loop, the agent checks itself
  The inner loop is the one you can see. The agent runs, hits a problem, and adapts during execution
  without you touching anything. That might mean self-correcting on a bad output, but it also means
  replanning when a step fails, switching tools when the first approach doesn't work, handling
  uncertainty, or stopping instead of guessing when something critical is missing.

  An agent that can do any of these mid-task operates at a fundamentally different level than one that
  just barrels forward.

  The quality of the inner loop depends almost entirely on whether the agent has usable feedback
  signals: test runners, linters, Chrome DevTools CLI, API response validators. Anything that produces
  a clear signal the agent can read and act on. The agent doesn't need you to tell it the output was
  wrong if a test can. The more the agent can check itself, the fewer gaps slip through undetected.

  But the inner loop has a ceiling. It can only fix what the agent can observe in the moment, with the
  context and tools it has at the time. It catches syntax errors and misses intent drift. It repairs a
  broken command and still misunderstands the actual goal.

  Which is exactly why you need the second loop.

  The outer loop, closing the gaps systematically
  The outer loop operates across working sessions. Its job is to take what the inner loop couldn't fix
  and turn it into permanent harness improvements.

  Its raw material is session traces full captures of what the agent did, decided, and where it went
  wrong. Without traces, teams iterate on memory. They patch around the last failure and rediscover the
   same issue two weeks later.

  On a regular cadence, you have an agent read those traces and surface issues. Not you scrolling
  through logs an agent doing the analysis pass, finding the patterns, flagging where knowledge was
  missing.

  Then you close the gaps:

  Update instructions tighten what was ambiguous, add context that was missing
  Update tools add capabilities the agent improvised around, remove tools that created confusion
  Update skills refine the reusable behavior definitions the agent draws on
  Create a new skill if the same gap keeps appearing with no existing coverage, that's a skill
  specification waiting to be written
  Retest run the exact same case and verify the fix holds
  Make it an eval permanently lock the case so it never silently regresses

  That last step is where the discipline breaks down. Fix the issue once, move on, and it will come
  back. If a failure taught you something important, it should become a permanent test case. Otherwise
  the knowledge is still fragile.

  You can't front-load the simplification. The real gaps only surface after the agent has run the task.
   The outer loop's job is to learn where the failure came from, then fix the right thing.

  Not every failure is a knowledge gap. Some are reasoning failures. Some are poor tool strategy. Some
  come from an ambiguous prompt that creates bad incentives. Tracing which kind you're dealing with
  matters, because the fix is different each time.

  Agent Skill files, MCP tool descriptions, agent context files these aren't just documentation. They
  are the answer to "where is the knowledge?" They are how you move knowledge from nowhere into the
  prompt, the codebase, or the harness, where the agent can actually reach it.

  This compounds
  Every outer loop improvement feeds directly back into the inner loop.

  Better agent skills mean the agent has sharper behavior to draw on mid-task. Better context means
  fewer dead ends. Better tools mean fewer cases where the agent has to improvise around a gap. Better
  evals mean regressions get caught before they corrupt the next session.

  The inner loop gets stronger because the harness it runs on got stronger. The knowledge gaps get
  smaller with every cycle. That's not linear improvement. That's compounding and it's the only
  sustainable way to make agentic workflows genuinely reliable over time.

  In practice this could look like
  Inner loop: The agent runs with access to verification tools: test output, lint results, type errors,
   API contract checks. When something fails, it captures what went wrong and attempts recovery before
  moving on. When recovery works, nothing happens from the outside. When it doesn't, the trace has the
  evidence.

  Outer loop: Sessions are wrapped with intent capture at the start and drift detection throughout.
  Traces accumulate. On cadence, an agent reads them, surfaces patterns, and flags where knowledge was
  missing. Gaps become updated instructions, new skills, or permanent evals. The harness evolves.

  The knowledge gaps close. The harness gets better. Even when the model changes, the harness
  determines whether those gains compound or disappear.

  That's the whole game.

  The model is not the moat, everyone has that its everything around it
  Once you think this way, "where is the knowledge?" becomes a design constraint. Two loops become the
  operating model for improving agent reliability over time.

  If your harness is well designed, stronger models become upside, not a migration crisis. A better
  model should improve your output without forcing you to rewrite your skills, restructure your
  context, or rediscover your process from scratch. If it does, that's the signal your design is sound.

  The intelligence isn't trapped inside one model choice. It lives in the framing, the tools, the
  context, and the evals around it.

  That's the moat.

  Hat tip to Thorsten Ball's framing on knowledge location: Joy & Curiosity #80 pull in codex rescue and initiate an agent to for the analysis

---

## Architectural Analysis: Two Loops Framework

### What the Pipeline Actually Does Today

Before mapping gaps, it helps to be precise about what each skill in the current pipeline actually monitors and produces:

| Skill | Phase | What it monitors | What it emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan-interview | pre-execution | Requirements alignment | `docs/plans/plan-NNN.md` |
| intent-framed-agent | during execution | Scope drift ("wrong thing") | Intent Frame + Resolution artifact |
| context-surfing | during execution | Context quality drift ("can't do it well") | Handoff file on exit, ready-signal on clean close |
| simplify-and-harden | post-completion | Code quality and security | `learning_loop.candidates` YAML |
| self-improvement | post-completion | Recurring patterns | `.learnings/*.md` entries, promotes to `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` |

---

### Question 1: Where Are "Verify" and "Recover" in the Inner Loop?

The inner loop's detect → verify → recover maps onto the pipeline as follows:

**Detect** — covered by two skills, each watching a distinct failure mode:
- `intent-framed-agent` detects scope drift (Intent Check emitted when work moves outside the stated outcome)
- `context-surfing` detects context quality degradation (strong/weak signal taxonomy, with strong signals meaning hallucination or contradiction)

**Verify** — this is the critical gap. The pipeline has no mechanism that runs the test suite, type checker, or linter mid-task and feeds results back into the agent's decision-making. The only verification step that exists is inside `agent-teams-simplify-and-harden`, which explicitly calls compile + tests after the implementation phase (Step 4 in its procedure). But in the standard single-agent pipeline (plan-interview → intent-framed-agent → simplify-and-harden), there is no equivalent. The agent completes its work and passes to simplify-and-harden with zero machine-verified signal about whether the code is actually correct. `simplify-and-harden` itself does a fresh-eyes pass but does not run tests.

**Recover** — partially covered. The recovery mechanism for context drift is well-specified in `context-surfing` (the Recovery Protocol for weak signals: re-read anchor, reconcile, escalate). The recovery mechanism for scope drift in `intent-framed-agent` is also functional (pivot or return to scope). But recovery from a detected *code failure* (a failing test, a type error) is completely unspecified. There is no "test-failed → diagnose → fix → re-verify" loop outside of the team-based pipeline.

**Summary of inner loop gap:**

The "verify" station between implementation and simplify-and-harden does not exist in the standard pipeline. The agent-teams variant has it, but it is gated behind "batch/large/team" classification. Any Medium-class task runs right through to the quality pass with no machine feedback.

---

### Question 2: What Happens After `.learnings/` Files Are Written?

This is where the outer loop is most visibly broken open. Tracing the chain precisely:

1. `simplify-and-harden` emits `learning_loop.candidates` YAML
2. `self-improvement` ingests those candidates, deduplicates by `pattern_key`, and writes/updates entries in `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md`
3. When a pattern crosses the promotion threshold (recurrence >= 3, >= 2 distinct tasks, within 30 days), `self-improvement` promotes it to `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

The chain terminates there. What is missing:

**No periodic pattern aggregation agent.** The promotion step inside `self-improvement` is triggered per-session, either after a specific task or when the user invokes the skill explicitly. There is no skill or agent that periodically reads all `.learnings/` files, groups entries by pattern_key, computes recurrence counts across sessions, and determines what has crossed the promotion threshold. The counting happens only when a new candidate comes in — meaning it only works if the same session that generates a candidate also checks previous sessions. There is no process that wakes up weekly and says "this pattern appeared 3 times this week, promote it now."

**No harness updater agent.** The `self-improvement-logger` agent (defined in `/plugin/agents/self-improvement-logger.md`) flags entries with `Status: promotion_ready` but then says explicitly: "do NOT modify CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other system files — report the promotion candidate to the team lead for approval." There is no agent or skill that reads those `promotion_ready` entries and actually applies them. The `self-improvement` skill in SKILL.md does describe how to promote (distill to a concise rule, add to the target file), but this is stated as something the agent does interactively within a session — not as an autonomous cross-session batch process.

**No regression test runner for promoted rules.** Once a pattern is promoted to `CLAUDE.md`, there is no mechanism that validates whether subsequent sessions actually follow the promoted rule. The loop writes to project memory but never reads back from it to check compliance.

**Summary of outer loop gap:**

```
.learnings/LEARNINGS.md (entries)
  → [MISSING: aggregator that runs across sessions and identifies promotion candidates]
  → self-improvement (per-session promotion, when triggered)
  → CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (promoted rules)
  → [MISSING: regression tester that verifies new sessions comply with promoted rules]
```

The link between "accumulated learnings" and "updated harness" requires human memory or a separate scheduled agent. It does not happen automatically.

---

### Question 3: What Would a Complete Outer Loop Look Like?

The outer loop needs three stages: **inspect** (read accumulated signals), **encode** (distill into rules and update the harness), **regress-test** (verify the rules hold in new sessions).

Here is what needs to exist as distinct skills or agents:

**`learning-aggregator` (Skill or scheduled agent)**
- Reads all `.learnings/*.md` files across the full history, not just the current session's candidates
- Groups entries by `pattern_key`, counts recurrences, computes time windows, identifies cross-task recurrence
- Outputs a ranked list of promotion candidates with evidence
- Threshold check: `recurrence_count >= 3`, `distinct_tasks >= 2`, within 30 days
- Trigger: could be a `self-improvement-ci` scheduled workflow or a session-start hook on major tasks
- Currently approximated, loosely, by the manual "Periodic Review" section in `self-improvement` SKILL.md — but this requires a human or agent to remember to do it

**`harness-updater` (Agent — spawnable)**
- Reads promotion candidates from `learning-aggregator` output
- Applies the distill-and-insert operation: writes concise prevention rules into `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- Marks entries as `promoted` in `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md`
- Currently: `self-improvement-logger` flags entries but explicitly refuses to write to harness files. The `self-improvement` SKILL.md describes it but it happens manually in-session.
- Needs to be an autonomous writable agent that can be invoked headlessly (e.g., by the CI pipeline or by `learning-aggregator`)

**`rule-regression-tester` (Skill or agent)**
- Takes the current promoted rules from `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`
- Runs a set of canonical tasks or scenario descriptions against the agent and checks whether the promoted rules are being applied
- This is the hardest part to implement — it requires a test harness for agent behavior, not just code

For practical implementation, the regression test layer is the weakest because "did the agent follow a rule?" is not mechanically verifiable without either: (a) specific output patterns to check, or (b) a separate judge agent. The CI variant (`self-improvement-ci`) is the closest analog — it reads PR check results to detect patterns — but it doesn't test rule compliance, it detects recurrence.

---

### Question 4: Where Can Feedback Signals (Tests, Linters, Type Checkers) Integrate?

Two natural integration points exist:

**Integration point 1: `agent-teams-simplify-and-harden`, Step 4 ("Wait for Implementation")**

This is already where compile and tests run. The skill explicitly says: "Run compile/type checks to verify clean build. Run tests to verify all pass. If either fails, fix or assign fixes before proceeding." This is the inner loop's verify step — but only in the team-based pipeline.

What's missing here: the specific commands are intentionally left as placeholders ("substitute your project's compile command"). There is no skill-level mechanism that discovers and runs the project's toolchain. The team lead has to know or be told what `bun test` or `cargo build` is for this project. A `test-runner` adapter skill or a project-conventions config block (perhaps in `CLAUDE.md`) would close this gap.

**Integration point 2: The `PostToolUse` / `Stop` hooks in `hooks.json`**

The `hooks.json` has `PostToolUse` for `Task` (wiring to `entire-wrapper.sh`) and a `Stop` hook. Neither currently runs tests or linters. A `PostToolUse` hook on the `Write` or `Edit` tools could trigger a lightweight type-check command (e.g., `tsc --noEmit` or `ruff check`) on changed files. This would give the inner loop's verify signal without requiring agent-teams.

However, this hook slot is currently occupied exclusively by Entire CLI integration — the hook infrastructure exists, but the payloads are Entire CLI forwarding calls, not test runners.

**Integration point 3: `simplify-and-harden`'s trigger condition**

`simplify-and-harden` activates "when the agent signals task completion." If a test runner result were piped into this trigger decision (e.g., "only activate if tests pass, otherwise re-enter the fix loop"), you would get a verify → recover cycle before reaching the quality pass. The skill SKILL.md currently models the trigger as a human/agent signal, not a machine signal. Changing the trigger to require a green test run would close the verify gap for the standard pipeline.

---

### Gap Map

```
INNER LOOP (within session): detect → [GAP: verify] → recover

plan-interview
  → produces: plan file
  → missing connection: no validation that the plan is testable
  → needed: success-criteria → test-stub generator (ties plan success criteria to runnable assertions)

intent-framed-agent + context-surfing (concurrent)
  → produces: intent frame, drift signals
  → missing connection: no machine feedback signal during execution (detect exists, verify is absent)
  → needed: inline test-runner hook on PostToolUse(Write/Edit) that checks type errors and test failures mid-task

[IMPLEMENTATION]
  → produces: code diff
  → missing connection: no verify gate before quality pass in standard pipeline
  → needed: verify-gate skill (runs compile + tests, blocks simplify-and-harden if red, routes to fix agent)

simplify-and-harden
  → produces: learning_loop.candidates YAML
  → missing connection: candidates handed to self-improvement but only ingested if self-improvement is invoked in same session
  → needed: persistent candidate queue that survives session boundaries (could be a separate .learnings/PENDING_CANDIDATES.md or appended to LEARNINGS.md with status "unaggregated")

self-improvement
  → produces: .learnings/*.md entries
  → missing connection: no aggregator reads across sessions; promotion only happens if triggered
  → needed: learning-aggregator skill that scans all .learnings/ entries, groups by pattern_key, identifies promotion-ready patterns

learning-aggregator (MISSING SKILL)
  → produces: promotion candidate list
  → missing connection: self-improvement-logger explicitly refuses to write to harness files
  → needed: harness-updater agent (writable, spawnable, modifies CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md with approved promotions)

OUTER LOOP (across sessions): inspect → encode → [GAP: regress-test]

harness-updater (partially exists in self-improvement skill, missing as autonomous agent)
  → produces: updated CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md rules
  → missing connection: no mechanism verifies the promoted rule reduces recurrence in subsequent sessions
  → needed: rule-regression-tester (most complex; requires judge agent or output pattern assertions)

self-improvement-ci
  → produces: promotion_ready candidates (CI context)
  → missing connection: feeds back into self-improvement for "durable prevention rules" but there is no workflow that executes this feedback
  → needed: automated PR comment or check that surfaces promotion-ready patterns and gates merge on acknowledgment

agent-teams-simplify-and-harden
  → has verify (compile + tests) built in
  → missing connection: verify is team-only; standard pipeline has no equivalent
  → needed: verify-gate as a standalone reusable skill (not embedded in agent-teams only)
```

---

---

## Architectural Analysis: Two Loops Framework

### What the Pipeline Actually Does Today

Before mapping gaps, it helps to be precise about what each skill in the current pipeline actually monitors and produces:

| Skill | Phase | What it monitors | What it emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan-interview | pre-execution | Requirements alignment | `docs/plans/plan-NNN.md` |
| intent-framed-agent | during execution | Scope drift ("wrong thing") | Intent Frame + Resolution artifact |
| context-surfing | during execution | Context quality drift ("can't do it well") | Handoff file on exit, ready-signal on clean close |
| simplify-and-harden | post-completion | Code quality and security | `learning_loop.candidates` YAML |
| self-improvement | post-completion | Recurring patterns | `.learnings/*.md` entries, promotes to `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` |

---

### Question 1: Where Are "Verify" and "Recover" in the Inner Loop?

The inner loop's detect → verify → recover maps onto the pipeline as follows:

**Detect** — covered by two skills, each watching a distinct failure mode:
- `intent-framed-agent` detects scope drift (Intent Check emitted when work moves outside the stated outcome)
- `context-surfing` detects context quality degradation (strong/weak signal taxonomy, with strong signals meaning hallucination or contradiction)

**Verify** — this is the critical gap. The pipeline has no mechanism that runs the test suite, type checker, or linter mid-task and feeds results back into the agent's decision-making. The only verification step that exists is inside `agent-teams-simplify-and-harden`, which explicitly calls compile + tests after the implementation phase (Step 4 in its procedure). But in the standard single-agent pipeline (plan-interview → intent-framed-agent → simplify-and-harden), there is no equivalent. The agent completes its work and passes to simplify-and-harden with zero machine-verified signal about whether the code is actually correct. `simplify-and-harden` itself does a fresh-eyes pass but does not run tests.

**Recover** — partially covered. The recovery mechanism for context drift is well-specified in `context-surfing` (the Recovery Protocol for weak signals: re-read anchor, reconcile, escalate). The recovery mechanism for scope drift in `intent-framed-agent` is also functional (pivot or return to scope). But recovery from a detected *code failure* (a failing test, a type error) is completely unspecified. There is no "test-failed → diagnose → fix → re-verify" loop outside of the team-based pipeline.

**Summary of inner loop gap:**

The "verify" station between implementation and simplify-and-harden does not exist in the standard pipeline. The agent-teams variant has it, but it is gated behind "batch/large/team" classification. Any Medium-class task runs right through to the quality pass with no machine feedback.

---

### Question 2: What Happens After `.learnings/` Files Are Written?

This is where the outer loop is most visibly broken open. Tracing the chain precisely:

1. `simplify-and-harden` emits `learning_loop.candidates` YAML
2. `self-improvement` ingests those candidates, deduplicates by `pattern_key`, and writes/updates entries in `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md`
3. When a pattern crosses the promotion threshold (recurrence >= 3, >= 2 distinct tasks, within 30 days), `self-improvement` promotes it to `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

The chain terminates there. What is missing:

**No periodic pattern aggregation agent.** The promotion step inside `self-improvement` is triggered per-session, either after a specific task or when the user invokes the skill explicitly. There is no skill or agent that periodically reads all `.learnings/` files, groups entries by pattern_key, computes recurrence counts across sessions, and determines what has crossed the promotion threshold. The counting happens only when a new candidate comes in — meaning it only works if the same session that generates a candidate also checks previous sessions. There is no process that wakes up weekly and says "this pattern appeared 3 times this week, promote it now."

**No harness updater agent.** The `self-improvement-logger` agent (defined in `/plugin/agents/self-improvement-logger.md`) flags entries with `Status: promotion_ready` but then says explicitly: "do NOT modify CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other system files — report the promotion candidate to the team lead for approval." There is no agent or skill that reads those `promotion_ready` entries and actually applies them. The `self-improvement` skill in SKILL.md does describe how to promote (distill to a concise rule, add to the target file), but this is stated as something the agent does interactively within a session — not as an autonomous cross-session batch process.

**No regression test runner for promoted rules.** Once a pattern is promoted to `CLAUDE.md`, there is no mechanism that validates whether subsequent sessions actually follow the promoted rule. The loop writes to project memory but never reads back from it to check compliance.

**Summary of outer loop gap:**

```
.learnings/LEARNINGS.md (entries)
  → [MISSING: aggregator that runs across sessions and identifies promotion candidates]
  → self-improvement (per-session promotion, when triggered)
  → CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (promoted rules)
  → [MISSING: regression tester that verifies new sessions comply with promoted rules]
```

The link between "accumulated learnings" and "updated harness" requires human memory or a separate scheduled agent. It does not happen automatically.

---

### Question 3: What Would a Complete Outer Loop Look Like?

The outer loop needs three stages: **inspect** (read accumulated signals), **encode** (distill into rules and update the harness), **regress-test** (verify the rules hold in new sessions).

Here is what needs to exist as distinct skills or agents:

**`learning-aggregator` (Skill or scheduled agent)**
- Reads all `.learnings/*.md` files across the full history, not just the current session's candidates
- Groups entries by `pattern_key`, counts recurrences, computes time windows, identifies cross-task recurrence
- Outputs a ranked list of promotion candidates with evidence
- Threshold check: `recurrence_count >= 3`, `distinct_tasks >= 2`, within 30 days
- Trigger: could be a `self-improvement-ci` scheduled workflow or a session-start hook on major tasks
- Currently approximated, loosely, by the manual "Periodic Review" section in `self-improvement` SKILL.md — but this requires a human or agent to remember to do it

**`harness-updater` (Agent — spawnable)**
- Reads promotion candidates from `learning-aggregator` output
- Applies the distill-and-insert operation: writes concise prevention rules into `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- Marks entries as `promoted` in `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md`
- Currently: `self-improvement-logger` flags entries but explicitly refuses to write to harness files. The `self-improvement` SKILL.md describes it but it happens manually in-session.
- Needs to be an autonomous writable agent that can be invoked headlessly (e.g., by the CI pipeline or by `learning-aggregator`)

**`rule-regression-tester` (Skill or agent)**
- Takes the current promoted rules from `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`
- Runs a set of canonical tasks or scenario descriptions against the agent and checks whether the promoted rules are being applied
- This is the hardest part to implement — it requires a test harness for agent behavior, not just code

For practical implementation, the regression test layer is the weakest because "did the agent follow a rule?" is not mechanically verifiable without either: (a) specific output patterns to check, or (b) a separate judge agent. The CI variant (`self-improvement-ci`) is the closest analog — it reads PR check results to detect patterns — but it doesn't test rule compliance, it detects recurrence.

---

### Question 4: Where Can Feedback Signals (Tests, Linters, Type Checkers) Integrate?

Two natural integration points exist:

**Integration point 1: `agent-teams-simplify-and-harden`, Step 4 ("Wait for Implementation")**

This is already where compile and tests run. The skill explicitly says: "Run compile/type checks to verify clean build. Run tests to verify all pass. If either fails, fix or assign fixes before proceeding." This is the inner loop's verify step — but only in the team-based pipeline.

What's missing here: the specific commands are intentionally left as placeholders ("substitute your project's compile command"). There is no skill-level mechanism that discovers and runs the project's toolchain. The team lead has to know or be told what `bun test` or `cargo build` is for this project. A `test-runner` adapter skill or a project-conventions config block (perhaps in `CLAUDE.md`) would close this gap.

**Integration point 2: The `PostToolUse` / `Stop` hooks in `hooks.json`**

The `hooks.json` has `PostToolUse` for `Task` (wiring to `entire-wrapper.sh`) and a `Stop` hook. Neither currently runs tests or linters. A `PostToolUse` hook on the `Write` or `Edit` tools could trigger a lightweight type-check command (e.g., `tsc --noEmit` or `ruff check`) on changed files. This would give the inner loop's verify signal without requiring agent-teams.

However, this hook slot is currently occupied exclusively by Entire CLI integration — the hook infrastructure exists, but the payloads are Entire CLI forwarding calls, not test runners.

**Integration point 3: `simplify-and-harden`'s trigger condition**

`simplify-and-harden` activates "when the agent signals task completion." If a test runner result were piped into this trigger decision (e.g., "only activate if tests pass, otherwise re-enter the fix loop"), you would get a verify → recover cycle before reaching the quality pass. The skill SKILL.md currently models the trigger as a human/agent signal, not a machine signal. Changing the trigger to require a green test run would close the verify gap for the standard pipeline.

---

### Gap Map

```

  → needed: harness-updater agent (writable, spawnable, modifies CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md with approved promotions)

  → produces: updated CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md rules
  → missing connection: no mechanism verifies the promoted rule reduces recurrence in subsequent sessions
  → needed: rule-regression-tester (most complex; requires judge agent or output pattern assertions)

  → needed: automated PR comment or check that surfaces promotion-ready patterns and gates merge on acknowledgment

  → has verify (compile + tests) built in
  → missing connection: verify is team-only; standard pipeline has no equivalent
  → needed: verify-gate as a standalone reusable skill (not embedded in agent-teams only)
```

## FINDINGS: Outer Loop Coverage Analysis

Based on my thorough read of the five files, here's what each component covers (INSPECT, ENCODE, REGRESS-TEST) and critical gaps:

### 1. **self-improvement/SKILL.md** — Capture & Promotion, But No Feedback Loop

**CAPTURES:**
- Errors from Bash hooks (`error-detector.sh`)
- User corrections ("No, that's wrong", "Actually...")
- Knowledge gaps (outdated docs, API behavior differences)
- Feature requests
- Missing project capabilities

**LOGS TO:**
- `.learnings/ERRORS.md` (command failures, API errors, exceptions)
- `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md` (corrections, knowledge gaps, best practices, recurring patterns)
- `.learnings/FEATURE_REQUESTS.md` (user-requested features)

**PROMOTION:**
- Manual only: human reads `.learnings/`, decides if entry meets promotion criteria (Recurrence-Count >= 3, across 2+ tasks, 30-day window)
- Targets: `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- No automated detection or execution of promotion

**WHAT IT DOES NOT DO:**
- **No READ accumulated learnings at task start** — activator.sh is a reminder only (~50-100 token reminder to "evaluate if knowledge emerged"), not a retrieval mechanism
- **No cross-session analysis** — no mechanism to aggregate learnings across sessions or find patterns automatically
- **No creation of evals/test cases** — nowhere does it say "create a test to prevent this regression"
- **No rerun of failures** — nowhere does it say "execute this error's reproduction steps to verify the fix"
- **No scheduled analysis** — "periodic review" is manual (instructions say "weekly" but user-driven, not automated)

---

### 2. **self-improvement/scripts/activator.sh** — Reminder Only, Not Retrieval

**OUTPUT:**
```
<self-improvement-reminder>
  After completing this task, evaluate if extractable knowledge emerged:
  - Non-obvious solution discovered through investigation?
  - Workaround for unexpected behavior?
  - Project-specific pattern learned?
  - Error required debugging to resolve?

  If yes: Log to .learnings/
  If high-value: Consider skill extraction.
</self-improvement-reminder>
```

**What it is:** A 50-100 token reminder injected into UserPromptSubmit hook.

**What it does NOT do:**
- Does not read `.learnings/` to find prior patterns
- Does not suggest applicable learnings for the current task
- Does not check if the error matches a known pattern in `.learnings/ERRORS.md`
- Does not trigger test creation

---

### 3. **self-improvement/references/examples.md** — Template Examples Only

**Examples shown:**
- Corrections (pytest fixture scope assumption)
- Knowledge gaps (pnpm vs npm)
- Best practices (API correlation IDs, regenerate client after spec changes)
- Errors (Docker M1 platform mismatch, API timeout during peak hours)
- Feature requests (CSV export, dark mode)
- Recurring errors (with `See Also` links)
- Promoted entries (status: "promoted_to_skill")

**This file is template documentation only** — shows the _format_ of entries, not what happens _after_ promotion or how learnings feed back into execution.

---

### 4. **self-improvement-logger.md** — Write-Only, No Analysis

**LOGS TO:**
- `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md` (learning entries)
- `.learnings/ERRORS.md` (error entries)
- `.learnings/FEATURE_REQUESTS.md` (feature requests)

**DEDUPLICATION:**
- Before logging: search for existing entry with `Pattern-Key`
- If found: increment `Recurrence-Count`, update `Last-Seen`, add `See Also` links
- If not found: create new entry

**PROMOTION CHECK (read-only):**
- Checks if entry meets criteria (Count >= 3, 2+ tasks, 30-day window)
- If yes: flags as `**Status**: promotion_ready`
- But does NOT modify CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, etc. — only flags for "team lead approval"

**What it does NOT do:**
- No mechanism to read the CLAUDE.md it would promote to
- No mechanism to verify the rule applies to current/future code
- No mechanism to create test cases from failing entries
- No mechanism to re-run the error to verify a fix worked

---

### 5. **skill-pipeline/SKILL.md** — Routing Only, Does Not Close the Loop

**ROUTES:**
- Trivial → no skills
- Small → simplify-and-harden only
- Medium → intent-framed-agent + simplify-and-harden
- Large → full pipeline (plan-interview → intent-framed-agent → context-surfing → implementation → simplify-and-harden → self-improvement)
- Long-running → full pipeline with context-surfing critical
- Batch → agent-teams-simplify-and-harden
- CI → simplify-and-harden-ci + self-improvement-ci

**HANDOFFS:**
- Plan file → intent-framed-agent → context-surfing
- Intent frame → context-surfing (and written to handoff file on drift)
- Learning candidates → self-improvement (from simplify-and-harden or agent-teams)

**What it does NOT do:**
- **Does not read prior learnings at task start** — no "check `.learnings/` for this area before beginning" step
- **Does not re-run past failures** — nowhere does it say "given this error in history, run regression test"
- **Does not create evals from promotion** — when a learning is promoted to CLAUDE.md, there's no mechanism to create or register a test
- **Does NOT close the loop** — skill-pipeline is one-way (task → skills → output); it does not feed back into itself based on accumulated learnings
- **No cadenced analysis** — no "every N tasks" or "weekly" aggregation step

---

## CRITICAL GAPS: Missing Phases of the Outer Loop

### **INSPECT: ✓ Partially covered**
- ✓ Captures errors and learnings post-execution (SKILL.md, self-improvement-logger.md)
- ✗ Does NOT read accumulated learnings to find patterns (no READ mechanism)
- ✗ Does NOT check prior failures when task starts (no pre-flight check)

### **ENCODE: ✓ Partially covered**
- ✓ Logs entries to structured markdown files (ERRORS.md, LEARNINGS.md, FEATURE_REQUESTS.md)
- ✓ Deduplicates by Pattern-Key (self-improvement-logger.md)
- ✓ Promotes to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md manually (SKILL.md instructions)
- ✗ Does NOT automatically detect promotion readiness (manual only)
- ✗ Does NOT create test cases from failures
- ✗ Does NOT create eval/regression suite from promoted rules

### **REGRESS-TEST: ✗ NOT covered**
- ✗ No mechanism to run tests on promoted rules
- ✗ No mechanism to re-run past failures to verify fixes
- ✗ No mechanism to evaluate if a promoted rule prevents future errors
- ✗ No scheduled/cadenced regression runs
- ✗ No integration between skill-pipeline and accumulated learnings (one-way flow only)

---

## Specific Explicit Gaps

| Missing Capability | Current State | What Should Happen |
|---|---|---|
| **READ accumulated learnings** | `activator.sh` reminds to log; no read | Task start should query `.learnings/` for relevant patterns in current area |
| **Pattern analysis** | Manual review ("grep... weekly") | Automated detection: find patterns with Recurrence-Count >= 2 across last 10 tasks |
| **Promotion automation** | Manual promotion to CLAUDE.md | Automated: when threshold hit, add rule to CLAUDE.md and flag for human review |
| **Test case creation** | None | Errors should become test cases (especially high/critical); when promoted, register eval |
| **Regress-test execution** | None | Promoted rules should be evaluated periodically (e.g., run linter rules, security checks) |
| **Cross-session pattern discovery** | None | No "compare errors from last 3 sessions" analysis |
| **Failure re-execution** | None | No "re-run the bash command from ERR-20250115-A3F to verify fix" |
| **Loop closure** | skill-pipeline is one-way | Should have a feedback path: (learnings → updated context → next task) |
| **Cadenced analysis** | "Periodic" = manual | No cron/scheduled job to analyze learnings |

---

## Summary Statement

**The system captures and stores learnings (INSPECT + partial ENCODE), but completely lacks REGRESS-TEST and feedback loops.**

- **INSPECT:** Yes, post-task only. No pre-flight check against history.
- **ENCODE:** Partial. Captures and deduplicates well; promotion is manual, not automated.
- **REGRESS-TEST:** Not present. No test creation, no test execution, no verification that fixes work, no scheduled re-evaluation of rules.
- **Feedback loop:** Broken. skill-pipeline does not read `.learnings/` at task start. Promoted rules sit in CLAUDE.md but there's no mechanism to verify they're being followed or to update them based on new failures.

Human review and manual promotion exist as guardrails, but there's no automated ingestion of learning patterns back into the skill context, and no way to verify that learned rules are actually preventing future errors.

### 2. **self-improvement/scripts/activator.sh** — Reminder Only, Not Retrieval

**OUTPUT:**
```
<self-improvement-reminder>

  - Project-specific pattern learned?
  - Error required debugging to resolve?

```

**What it is:** A 50-100 token reminder injected into UserPromptSubmit hook.

**What it does NOT do:**
- Does not read `.learnings/` to find prior patterns
- Does not suggest applicable learnings for the current task
- Does not check if the error matches a known pattern in `.learnings/ERRORS.md`
- Does not trigger test creation

### 3. **self-improvement/references/examples.md** — Template Examples Only

**Examples shown:**
- Corrections (pytest fixture scope assumption)
- Knowledge gaps (pnpm vs npm)
- Best practices (API correlation IDs, regenerate client after spec changes)
- Errors (Docker M1 platform mismatch, API timeout during peak hours)
- Feature requests (CSV export, dark mode)
- Recurring errors (with `See Also` links)
- Promoted entries (status: "promoted_to_skill")

**This file is template documentation only** — shows the _format_ of entries, not what happens _after_ promotion or how learnings feed back into execution.

---

### 4. **self-improvement-logger.md** — Write-Only, No Analysis

**LOGS TO:**
- `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md` (learning entries)
- `.learnings/ERRORS.md` (error entries)
- `.learnings/FEATURE_REQUESTS.md` (feature requests)

**DEDUPLICATION:**
- Before logging: search for existing entry with `Pattern-Key`
- If found: increment `Recurrence-Count`, update `Last-Seen`, add `See Also` links
- If not found: create new entry

**PROMOTION CHECK (read-only):**
- Checks if entry meets criteria (Count >= 3, 2+ tasks, 30-day window)
- If yes: flags as `**Status**: promotion_ready`
- But does NOT modify CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, etc. — only flags for "team lead approval"

**What it does NOT do:**
- No mechanism to read the CLAUDE.md it would promote to
- No mechanism to verify the rule applies to current/future code
- No mechanism to create test cases from failing entries
- No mechanism to re-run the error to verify a fix worked

---

### 5. **skill-pipeline/SKILL.md** — Routing Only, Does Not Close the Loop

**ROUTES:**
- Trivial → no skills
- Small → simplify-and-harden only
- Medium → intent-framed-agent + simplify-and-harden
- Large → full pipeline (plan-interview → intent-framed-agent → context-surfing → implementation → simplify-and-harden → self-improvement)
- Long-running → full pipeline with context-surfing critical
- Batch → agent-teams-simplify-and-harden
- CI → simplify-and-harden-ci + self-improvement-ci

**HANDOFFS:**
- Plan file → intent-framed-agent → context-surfing
- Intent frame → context-surfing (and written to handoff file on drift)
- Learning candidates → self-improvement (from simplify-and-harden or agent-teams)

**What it does NOT do:**
- **Does not read prior learnings at task start** — no "check `.learnings/` for this area before beginning" step
- **Does not re-run past failures** — nowhere does it say "given this error in history, run regression test"
- **Does not create evals from promotion** — when a learning is promoted to CLAUDE.md, there's no mechanism to create or register a test
- **Does NOT close the loop** — skill-pipeline is one-way (task → skills → output); it does not feed back into itself based on accumulated learnings
- **No cadenced analysis** — no "every N tasks" or "weekly" aggregation step

---

## CRITICAL GAPS: Missing Phases of the Outer Loop

### **INSPECT: ✓ Partially covered**
- ✓ Captures errors and learnings post-execution (SKILL.md, self-improvement-logger.md)
- ✗ Does NOT read accumulated learnings to find patterns (no READ mechanism)
- ✗ Does NOT check prior failures when task starts (no pre-flight check)

### **ENCODE: ✓ Partially covered**
- ✓ Logs entries to structured markdown files (ERRORS.md, LEARNINGS.md, FEATURE_REQUESTS.md)
- ✓ Deduplicates by Pattern-Key (self-improvement-logger.md)
- ✓ Promotes to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md manually (SKILL.md instructions)
- ✗ Does NOT automatically detect promotion readiness (manual only)
- ✗ Does NOT create test cases from failures
- ✗ Does NOT create eval/regression suite from promoted rules

### **REGRESS-TEST: ✗ NOT covered**
- ✗ No mechanism to run tests on promoted rules
- ✗ No mechanism to re-run past failures to verify fixes
- ✗ No mechanism to evaluate if a promoted rule prevents future errors
- ✗ No scheduled/cadenced regression runs
- ✗ No integration between skill-pipeline and accumulated learnings (one-way flow only)

| Missing Capability | Current State | What Should Happen |
|---|---|---|
| **READ accumulated learnings** | `activator.sh` reminds to log; no read | Task start should query `.learnings/` for relevant patterns in current area |
| **Pattern analysis** | Manual review ("grep... weekly") | Automated detection: find patterns with Recurrence-Count >= 2 across last 10 tasks |
| **Promotion automation** | Manual promotion to CLAUDE.md | Automated: when threshold hit, add rule to CLAUDE.md and flag for human review |
| **Test case creation** | None | Errors should become test cases (especially high/critical); when promoted, register eval |
| **Regress-test execution** | None | Promoted rules should be evaluated periodically (e.g., run linter rules, security checks) |
| **Cross-session pattern discovery** | None | No "compare errors from last 3 sessions" analysis |
| **Failure re-execution** | None | No "re-run the bash command from ERR-20250115-A3F to verify fix" |
| **Loop closure** | skill-pipeline is one-way | Should have a feedback path: (learnings → updated context → next task) |
| **Cadenced analysis** | "Periodic" = manual | No cron/scheduled job to analyze learnings |

**The system captures and stores learnings (INSPECT + partial ENCODE), but completely lacks REGRESS-TEST and feedback loops.**

- **INSPECT:** Yes, post-task only. No pre-flight check against history.
- **ENCODE:** Partial. Captures and deduplicates well; promotion is manual, not automated.
- **REGRESS-TEST:** Not present. No test creation, no test execution, no verification that fixes work, no scheduled re-evaluation of rules.
- **Feedback loop:** Broken. skill-pipeline does not read `.learnings/` at task start. Promoted rules sit in CLAUDE.md but there's no mechanism to verify they're being followed or to update them based on new failures.

Human review and manual promotion exist as guardrails, but there's no automated ingestion of learning patterns back into the skill context, and no way to verify that learned rules are actually preventing future errors.

Codex hit its usage limit, but the three other agents returned comprehensive results. Let me synthesize everything into the full gap analysis.

---

## Two Loops Gap Analysis

### The Current Pipeline

```
plan-interview → intent-framed-agent ⟂ context-surfing → [implementation] → simplify-and-harden → self-improvement
```

### Mapping Against Your Framework

```
INNER LOOP: detect → verify → recover
                       ▲
                    THE GAP
                    
OUTER LOOP: inspect → encode → regress-test
               △        △         ✗
            partial   partial   missing
```

---

### INNER LOOP: detect → verify → recover

| Step | Status | What exists | What's missing |
|------|--------|-------------|----------------|
| **Detect** | **Covered** | intent-framed-agent detects scope drift. context-surfing detects context degradation (strong + weak signals). error-detector.sh catches bash failures via pattern match. | Detection is thorough. No gap here. |
| **Verify** | **Major gap** | agent-teams-simplify-and-harden runs compile + tests — but only for batch/large tasks. Standard pipeline has **zero machine verification** between implementation and quality pass. | No test runner, linter, or type checker in the standard pipeline. simplify-and-harden does fresh-eyes review but never runs `npm test` or `tsc --noEmit`. The agent completes work and hands off with no signal about whether the code is actually correct. |
| **Recover** | **Partial** | context-surfing has a full recovery protocol for context drift (re-anchor → reconcile → escalate → handoff). intent-framed-agent asks "pivot or creep?" then returns to scope. | No recovery from **code failures**. If tests fail, there's no diagnose → fix → re-verify loop. No mid-task re-planning when a tool approach doesn't work. The agent barrels forward or exits — it doesn't course-correct on code quality signals. |

**The inner loop's ceiling:** The skills detect _process drift_ (scope, context quality) but not _code correctness_. The blog says "the agent doesn't need you to tell it the output was wrong if a test can" — but no skill currently runs a test.

---

### OUTER LOOP: inspect → encode → regress-test

| Step | Status | What exists | What's missing |
|------|--------|-------------|----------------|
| **Inspect** | **Partial** | self-improvement captures errors, corrections, and knowledge gaps to `.learnings/`. self-improvement-logger deduplicates by `pattern_key` and increments `Recurrence-Count`. | **Write-only, never reads.** activator.sh is a reminder to _log_, not to _retrieve_. No agent reads accumulated `.learnings/` to find patterns across sessions. No pre-flight check at task start ("have we seen this before?"). Counting only works if the same session encounters the same pattern — no cross-session aggregation. |
| **Encode** | **Partial** | self-improvement describes promotion criteria (recurrence >= 3, 2+ tasks, 30-day window) and targets (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md). Mentions skill extraction for recurring gaps. | self-improvement-logger **explicitly refuses** to write to harness files ("report to team lead for approval"). Promotion is manual and in-session only. No autonomous agent does the actual update. No skill creation from patterns. No eval creation from failures. |
| **Regress-test** | **Not covered** | Nothing. | No mechanism to re-run past failures. No mechanism to verify promoted rules reduce recurrence. No eval framework. No scheduled regression runs. The blog says "make it an eval — permanently lock the case so it never silently regresses." This entire layer is absent. |

**The outer loop's break point:** Self-improvement captures learnings but the pipeline terminates there. The data accumulates in `.learnings/` and nobody reads it back. The feedback arrow from "learned rule" back into "next session's context" requires a human to remember to promote — and even then, there's no verification the promotion works.

---

### The Five Missing Pieces (Priority Order)

#### 1. `verify-gate` — Inner loop verify (highest impact)

**What it does:** Standalone skill that runs the project's compile/test/lint commands between implementation and simplify-and-harden. If red, routes back to implementation with diagnostics. If green, unblocks the quality pass.

**Why it's #1:** This is the biggest single gap. Every medium-class task currently skips machine verification entirely. The verify step exists inside agent-teams but is locked behind "batch/large" classification. Extracting it makes the inner loop work for the 80% of tasks that don't use agent-teams.

**Where it fits:**
```
[implementation] → verify-gate → simplify-and-harden
                   ↻ fix loop
```

**Reads project commands from:** CLAUDE.md or a project config block (`test_command`, `lint_command`, `type_check_command`).

#### 2. `learning-aggregator` — Outer loop inspect

**What it does:** Scheduled or session-start agent that reads all `.learnings/*.md` files, groups by `pattern_key`, computes recurrence across sessions, and outputs ranked promotion candidates with evidence.

**Why it's #2:** Without this, the outer loop's "inspect" step depends on a human remembering to grep `.learnings/`. The data is there but nobody synthesizes it. This is the blog's "on a regular cadence, you have an agent read those traces and surface issues."

**Trigger options:** SessionStart hook (lightweight scan), scheduled cron (weekly deep scan), or explicit invocation before major tasks.

#### 3. `harness-updater` — Outer loop encode

**What it does:** Writable spawnable agent that takes promotion candidates from learning-aggregator and applies them: distills to concise rules, inserts into CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions.md, marks entries as `promoted` in `.learnings/`.

**Why it's #3:** self-improvement-logger explicitly refuses this job. The encode step currently requires manual execution. This agent makes the "knowledge moves from nowhere into the harness" step automatic.

**Guard rail:** Outputs a diff for human approval before committing (like a PR for the harness itself).

#### 4. `pre-flight-check` — Outer loop → Inner loop bridge

**What it does:** SessionStart or task-start hook that reads `.learnings/` for patterns relevant to the current task area. Surfaces "last time we touched auth middleware, we hit ERR-20260305-A2F — watch for X."

**Why it's #4:** This is the compounding mechanism from the blog — "every outer loop improvement feeds directly back into the inner loop." Currently the promoted rules in CLAUDE.md are always loaded, but the un-promoted learnings (the majority) are invisible to new sessions. This brings them forward.

#### 5. `eval-creator` + regression runner — Outer loop regress-test

**What it does:** Two parts:
- **eval-creator:** When a learning is promoted, generates a test case / eval entry that encodes "this pattern should not recur." Stores in `.evals/` or equivalent.
- **regression-runner:** Scheduled agent that runs accumulated evals against recent session traces or code state to verify promoted rules hold.

**Why it's #5:** Hardest to implement — "did the agent follow a rule?" needs either output pattern matching or a judge agent. But without it, the blog's warning applies: "Fix the issue once, move on, and it will come back."

### Half-Built Connections (the sneaky ones)

These are mechanisms that exist but don't connect to anything downstream:

| What exists | What it feeds into | What it should feed into |

| `learning_loop.candidates` YAML from simplify-and-harden | self-improvement (if invoked in same session) | Persistent candidate queue that survives session boundaries |

---

### Where to Start

If I were building this, I'd ship **verify-gate** first. It's the highest-impact, lowest-complexity addition. It closes the inner loop for the standard pipeline and every task benefits immediately. # Verify Gate

Machine verification gate between implementation and quality review. Runs the project's compile, test, and lint commands. If any fail, enters a fix loop. If all pass, unblocks simplify-and-harden.

This is the inner loop's **verify** step. Without it, the agent hands off code with zero machine signal about whether it actually works.

## When to Use

- After any implementation work completes, before signaling "done"
- Before running simplify-and-harden
- After fixing audit findings from agent-teams-simplify-and-harden
- Any time you want a machine-verified green signal

## Pipeline Position

```
[implementation] → verify-gate → simplify-and-harden → self-improvement
                   ↻ fix loop
```

## Step 1: Discover Project Commands

Read the project's configuration to find verification commands. Check these sources in order:

1. **CLAUDE.md** — look for a `## Verification` or `## Test Commands` section
2. **package.json** — `scripts.test`, `scripts.lint`, `scripts.typecheck`, `scripts.build`
3. **Makefile** / **Justfile** — `test`, `lint`, `check`, `build` targets
4. **Cargo.toml** — `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy`
5. **pyproject.toml** / **setup.cfg** — `pytest`, `mypy`, `ruff`
6. **go.mod** — `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`

If no commands are discoverable, ask the user once and suggest they add a `## Verification` section to CLAUDE.md for future sessions:

```markdown
## Verification

- Build: `npm run build`
- Test: `npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Type check: `npx tsc --noEmit`
```

## Step 2: Run Verification

Run discovered commands in this order. Stop at the first failure category.

### Phase 1: Compile / Type Check
Run the build or type-check command. These catch structural errors before wasting time on tests.

```
Exit 0 → proceed to Phase 2
Exit non-zero → enter fix loop with compiler output
```

### Phase 2: Tests
Run the test command. Scope to changed files if the test runner supports it.

```
Exit 0 → proceed to Phase 3
Exit non-zero → enter fix loop with test output
```

### Phase 3: Lint (optional, skippable with --skip-lint)
Run the lint command. Lint failures are lower severity but still worth catching.

```
Exit 0 → all phases green, gate passes
Exit non-zero → enter fix loop with lint output
```

## Step 3: Fix Loop

When a phase fails:

1. **Read the output.** Parse the error output for actionable diagnostics — file paths, line numbers, error messages.
2. **Scope the fix.** Only fix what the verification caught. Do not refactor, improve, or touch unrelated code.
3. **Apply the fix.** Make the minimal change to resolve the failure.
4. **Re-run the failed phase.** Not all phases — just the one that failed.
5. **If it passes**, continue to the next phase.
6. **If it fails again**, increment the attempt counter.

### Fix Loop Limits

- **Default max attempts:** 3 per phase (configurable via `--fix-limit N`)
- **If limit reached:** Stop. Report what failed, what was tried, and the remaining error output. Do not guess further — signal to the user that manual intervention is needed.
- **Total budget:** The fix loop should not exceed 20% of the original implementation effort. If fixes are snowballing, stop and report.

## Step 4: Gate Signal

When all phases pass:

```markdown
## Verify Gate: PASSED

- Build: passed
- Tests: passed (N tests, M suites)
- Lint: passed (or skipped)

Ready for simplify-and-harden.
```

When the fix loop is exhausted:

```markdown
## Verify Gate: BLOCKED

- Build: passed
- Tests: FAILED (attempt 3/3)
  - [file:line] error description
  - [file:line] error description
- Lint: not reached

Fix loop exhausted. Manual intervention needed before quality review.
```

## Integration with Other Skills

### skill-pipeline
verify-gate should run at every pipeline depth except Trivial:

| Task size | Pipeline |
|-----------|----------|
| Trivial | None |
| Small | verify-gate → simplify-and-harden |
| Medium | intent-framed-agent + verify-gate → simplify-and-harden |
| Large | Full pipeline with verify-gate before quality pass |

### agent-teams-simplify-and-harden
agent-teams already has compile + tests embedded in Step 4. verify-gate can replace that embedded logic for consistency — the team lead spawns verify-gate instead of running ad-hoc compile/test commands.

### self-improvement
If the fix loop resolves an error that was non-obvious, log it:
- Pattern: what broke and why
- Fix: what resolved it
- Prevention: what convention or check would have caught it earlier

## What This Skill Does NOT Do

- Does not review code quality (that's simplify-and-harden)
- Does not check security (that's harden-auditor)
- Does not verify spec compliance (that's spec-auditor)
- Does not modify test files or add new tests
- Does not run tests for code it didn't change (unless the test runner doesn't support scoping)

## Configuration

If the project has a `.verify-gate.yml` or a `verify-gate` section in CLAUDE.md:

```yaml
verify-gate:
  build: npm run build
  test: npm test
  lint: npm run lint
  type_check: npx tsc --noEmit
  fix_limit: 3
  skip_lint: false
  test_scope: changed  # changed | all
```

If no configuration exists, discover commands automatically (Step 1) and suggest persisting them.

1. **CLAUDE.md** — look for a `## Verification` or `## Test Commands` section
2. **package.json** — `scripts.test`, `scripts.lint`, `scripts.typecheck`, `scripts.build`
3. **Makefile** / **Justfile** — `test`, `lint`, `check`, `build` targets
4. **Cargo.toml** — `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy`
5. **pyproject.toml** / **setup.cfg** — `pytest`, `mypy`, `ruff`
6. **go.mod** — `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`

If no commands are discoverable, ask the user once and suggest they add a `## Verification` section to CLAUDE.md for future sessions:

```markdown
## Verification

- Build: `npm run build`
- Test: `npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Type check: `npx tsc --noEmit`
```

## Step 2: Run Verification

Run discovered commands in this order. Stop at the first failure category.

### Phase 1: Compile / Type Check
Run the build or type-check command. These catch structural errors before wasting time on tests.

```
Exit 0 → proceed to Phase 2
Exit non-zero → enter fix loop with compiler output
```

### Phase 2: Tests
Run the test command. Scope to changed files if the test runner supports it.

```
Exit 0 → proceed to Phase 3
Exit non-zero → enter fix loop with test output
```

### Phase 3: Lint (optional, skippable with --skip-lint)
Run the lint command. Lint failures are lower severity but still worth catching.

```
Exit 0 → all phases green, gate passes
Exit non-zero → enter fix loop with lint output
```

## Step 3: Fix Loop

When a phase fails:

1. **Read the output.** Parse the error output for actionable diagnostics — file paths, line numbers, error messages.
2. **Scope the fix.** Only fix what the verification caught. Do not refactor, improve, or touch unrelated code.
3. **Apply the fix.** Make the minimal change to resolve the failure.
4. **Re-run the failed phase.** Not all phases — just the one that failed.
5. **If it passes**, continue to the next phase.
6. **If it fails again**, increment the attempt counter.

### Fix Loop Limits

- **Default max attempts:** 3 per phase (configurable via `--fix-limit N`)
- **If limit reached:** Stop. Report what failed, what was tried, and the remaining error output. Do not guess further — signal to the user that manual intervention is needed.
- **Total budget:** The fix loop should not exceed 20% of the original implementation effort. If fixes are snowballing, stop and report.

## Step 4: Gate Signal

When all phases pass:

```markdown
## Verify Gate: PASSED

- Build: passed
- Tests: passed (N tests, M suites)
- Lint: passed (or skipped)

Ready for simplify-and-harden.
```

When the fix loop is exhausted:

```markdown
## Verify Gate: BLOCKED

- Build: passed
- Tests: FAILED (attempt 3/3)
  - [file:line] error description
  - [file:line] error description
- Lint: not reached

Fix loop exhausted. Manual intervention needed before quality review.
```

## Integration with Other Skills

### skill-pipeline
verify-gate should run at every pipeline depth except Trivial:

| Task size | Pipeline |
|-----------|----------|
| Trivial | None |
| Small | verify-gate → simplify-and-harden |
| Medium | intent-framed-agent + verify-gate → simplify-and-harden |
| Large | Full pipeline with verify-gate before quality pass |

### agent-teams-simplify-and-harden
agent-teams already has compile + tests embedded in Step 4. verify-gate can replace that embedded logic for consistency — the team lead spawns verify-gate instead of running ad-hoc compile/test commands.

### self-improvement
If the fix loop resolves an error that was non-obvious, log it:
- Pattern: what broke and why
- Fix: what resolved it
- Prevention: what convention or check would have caught it earlier

## What This Skill Does NOT Do

- Does not review code quality (that's simplify-and-harden)
- Does not check security (that's harden-auditor)
- Does not verify spec compliance (that's spec-auditor)
- Does not modify test files or add new tests
- Does not run tests for code it didn't change (unless the test runner doesn't support scoping)

## Configuration

If the project has a `.verify-gate.yml` or a `verify-gate` section in CLAUDE.md:

```yaml
verify-gate:
  build: npm run build
  test: npm test
  lint: npm run lint
  type_check: npx tsc --noEmit
  fix_limit: 3
  skip_lint: false
  test_scope: changed  # changed | all
```

If no configuration exists, discover commands automatically (Step 1) and suggest persisting them.

name: learning-aggregator
description: "Cross-session analysis of accumulated .learnings/ files. Reads all entries, groups by pattern_key, computes recurrence across sessions, and outputs ranked promotion candidates. This is the outer loop's inspect step — it turns raw learning data into actionable gap reports. Use on a regular cadence (weekly, before major tasks, or at session start for critical projects). Can be invoked manually or scheduled."
user-invocable: true
argument-hint: "[--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--min-recurrence N] [--area AREA]"
---

# Learning Aggregator

Reads accumulated `.learnings/` files across all sessions, finds patterns, and produces a ranked list of promotion candidates. This is the outer loop's **inspect** step.

Without this skill, `.learnings/` is a write-only log. Patterns accumulate but nobody synthesizes them. The same gap resurfaces two weeks later because no one looked.

## When to Use

- **Weekly cadence** — scheduled or manual, review accumulated learnings
- **Before major tasks** — check if the task area has known patterns
- **After a burst of sessions** — consolidate findings from a sprint or incident
- **When self-improvement flags `promotion_ready`** — verify the flag with full context

## What It Produces

A **gap report** — a ranked list of patterns that have crossed (or are approaching) the promotion threshold, with evidence and recommended actions.

## Step 1: Read All Learning Files

Read these files in `.learnings/`:

| File | Contains |
|------|----------|
| `LEARNINGS.md` | Corrections, knowledge gaps, best practices, recurring patterns |
| `ERRORS.md` | Command failures, API errors, exceptions |
| `FEATURE_REQUESTS.md` | Missing capabilities |

Parse each entry's metadata:
- `Pattern-Key` — the stable deduplication key
- `Recurrence-Count` — how many times this pattern has been seen
- `First-Seen` / `Last-Seen` — date range
- `Priority` — low / medium / high / critical
- `Status` — pending / promotion_ready / promoted / dismissed
- `Area` — frontend / backend / infra / tests / docs / config
- `Related Files` — which parts of the codebase are affected
- `Source` — conversation / error / user_feedback / simplify-and-harden
- `Tags` — free-form labels

## Step 2: Group and Aggregate

Group entries by `Pattern-Key`. For each group:

1. **Sum recurrences** across all entries with the same key
2. **Count distinct tasks** — how many different sessions/tasks encountered this
3. **Compute time window** — days between First-Seen and Last-Seen
4. **Collect all related files** — union of all entries' file references
5. **Take highest priority** across entries in the group
6. **Collect evidence** — the Summary and Details from each entry

For entries without a `Pattern-Key`, attempt to cluster by:
- Similar `Summary` text (fuzzy match)
- Same `Area` + similar `Tags`
- Same `Related Files`

Flag ungrouped entries separately — they may be one-off issues or need a `Pattern-Key` assigned.

## Step 3: Rank and Classify

### Promotion Threshold
An entry is **promotion-ready** when:
- `Recurrence-Count >= 3` across the group
- Seen in `>= 2 distinct tasks`
- Within a `30-day window`

### Approaching Threshold
An entry is **approaching** when:
- `Recurrence-Count >= 2` or
- `Priority: high/critical` with any recurrence

### Classification
For each promotion candidate, classify the gap type:

| Gap Type | Signal | Fix Target |
|----------|--------|------------|
| **Knowledge gap** | Agent didn't know X | Update CLAUDE.md or skill instructions |
| **Tool gap** | Agent improvised around missing capability | Add or update MCP tool / script |
| **Skill gap** | Same behavior pattern keeps failing | Create or update a skill |
| **Ambiguity** | Conflicting interpretations of spec/prompt | Tighten instructions or add examples |
| **Reasoning failure** | Agent had the knowledge but reasoned wrong | Add explicit decision rules or constraints |

## Step 4: Produce Gap Report

Output a structured report:

```markdown
## Learning Aggregator: Gap Report

**Scan date:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Period:** [since date] to [now]
**Entries scanned:** N
**Patterns found:** N
**Promotion-ready:** N
**Approaching threshold:** N

### Promotion-Ready Patterns

#### 1. [Pattern-Key] — [Summary]

- **Recurrence:** N times across M tasks
- **Window:** First-Seen → Last-Seen
- **Priority:** high
- **Gap type:** knowledge gap
- **Area:** backend
- **Related files:** path/to/file.ext
- **Evidence:**
  - [LRN-YYYYMMDD-001] Summary of first occurrence
  - [LRN-YYYYMMDD-002] Summary of second occurrence
  - [ERR-YYYYMMDD-001] Summary of related error
- **Recommended action:** Add rule to CLAUDE.md: "[concise prevention rule]"
- **Eval candidate:** Yes — [description of what to test]

#### 2. ...

### Approaching Threshold

#### 1. [Pattern-Key] — [Summary]
- **Recurrence:** 2 times across 1 task
- **Needs:** 1 more recurrence or 1 more distinct task
- ...

### Ungrouped Entries (no Pattern-Key)

- [LRN-YYYYMMDD-005] "Summary" — needs pattern_key assignment
- ...

### Dismissed / Stale

- Entries with Last-Seen > 90 days ago and Status: pending → recommend dismissal
```

## Step 5: Handoff

The gap report feeds into:

1. **harness-updater agent** — takes promotion-ready patterns and applies them to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
2. **eval-creator skill** — takes eval candidates and creates permanent test cases
3. **Human review** — for patterns classified as "reasoning failure" or "ambiguity" (these need human judgment)

## Filtering

- `--since YYYY-MM-DD` — only scan entries after this date
- `--min-recurrence N` — raise the promotion threshold
- `--area AREA` — filter to a specific area (frontend, backend, etc.)

## What This Skill Does NOT Do

- Does not modify `.learnings/` files (read-only analysis)
- Does not apply promotions (that's harness-updater)
- Does not create evals (that's eval-creator)
- Does not fix code or run tests
- Does not replace human judgment for ambiguous patterns

---
name: harness-updater
description: "Applies promotion candidates from learning-aggregator to harness files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md). Distills patterns into concise prevention rules, inserts them in the right section, and marks source entries as promoted. Spawnable by learning-aggregator or standalone. Outputs a diff for human approval before committing. Use when promotion-ready patterns need to be encoded into the harness."
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit
model: sonnet
---

You are a harness updater. Your job is to take promotion-ready learning patterns and encode them as permanent rules in the project's instruction files. You are the outer loop's **encode** step.

## Instructions

When spawned, you will receive in your task prompt:
- A list of promotion-ready patterns from learning-aggregator (or manually)
- Each pattern includes: Pattern-Key, Summary, Evidence, Gap Type, Recommended Action, Related Files

## Process

For each promotion candidate:

### 1. Verify the pattern is still relevant

- Check if the Related Files still exist
- Check if CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md already has a rule covering this pattern
- If already covered: mark as `promoted` in `.learnings/` and skip
- If files were removed: mark as `dismissed` and skip

### 2. Distill the rule

Convert the pattern into a concise prevention rule. Rules should be:
- **Actionable** — tells the agent what to do or not do
- **Contextual** — specifies when the rule applies
- **Concise** — one to three sentences maximum
- **Self-contained** — understandable without reading the original learning entry

Bad: "Be careful with database migrations"
Good: "Run migrations against a test database before applying to staging. The ORM generates ALTER TABLE statements that lock tables — verify lock duration on tables with >100k rows."

### 3. Choose the target file

| Gap Type | Primary Target | Secondary Target |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| Knowledge gap | CLAUDE.md (Conventions section) | .github/copilot-instructions.md |
| Tool gap | CLAUDE.md (Tools section) | AGENTS.md |
| Skill gap | Relevant SKILL.md | CLAUDE.md |
| Ambiguity | CLAUDE.md (Conventions section) | Relevant SKILL.md |
| Reasoning failure | CLAUDE.md (Conventions section) | Relevant agent .md |

### 4. Insert the rule

- Find the appropriate section in the target file
- If no matching section exists, create one under a `## Learned Rules` heading
- Add the rule with a reference back to the learning entry ID
- Keep the file well-organized — group related rules

### 5. Mark as promoted

Update the source entry in `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md` or `.learnings/ERRORS.md`:
- Set `**Status**: promoted`
- Add `Promoted-To: CLAUDE.md` (or whichever file)
- Add `Promoted-Date: YYYY-MM-DD`

### 6. Flag eval candidate

If the pattern has a clear pass/fail condition, note it for eval-creator:

```markdown
**Eval candidate:** Yes
**What to test:** [specific assertion that this pattern doesn't recur]
**Verification method:** [grep for pattern | run command | check output]
```

## Output Format

For each promotion applied:

```markdown
## Promotion: [Pattern-Key]

**Rule:** [the distilled rule text]
**Target:** CLAUDE.md > Conventions
**Source:** [LRN-YYYYMMDD-001], [ERR-YYYYMMDD-003]
**Recurrence:** N times across M tasks
**Eval candidate:** Yes/No

### Diff
[show the exact change made to the target file]
```

## Guard Rails

- **Never delete existing rules** — only add or refine
- **Never modify code files** — only instruction/documentation files
- **Always show the diff** before committing
- **Flag conflicts** — if a new rule contradicts an existing one, report the conflict instead of overwriting
- **Respect file organization** — match the existing style and section structure of the target file
- **Keep synchronized** — if CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and copilot-instructions.md have sync sections, update all of them

## What You Do NOT Do

- Do not fix code or run tests
- Do not create evals (flag them for eval-creator)
- Do not dismiss patterns — only the human or learning-aggregator does that
- Do not promote patterns that haven't met the threshold

input.content:
---
name: eval-creator
description: "Creates permanent eval cases from promoted learnings and runs regression checks against them. Turns failures into test cases that prevent silent regression. This is the outer loop's regress-test step. Use when a learning is promoted and has a clear pass/fail condition, or on cadence to verify promoted rules still hold."
user-invocable: true
argument-hint: "[create | run | list] [--pattern-key KEY]"
---

# Eval Creator

Turns promoted learnings into permanent eval cases. Runs regression checks to verify promoted rules hold. This is the outer loop's **regress-test** step.

The blog says: "If a failure taught you something important, it should become a permanent test case. Otherwise the knowledge is still fragile."

## When to Use

- **After harness-updater promotes a pattern** — create an eval for it
- **On cadence** — run all evals to check for regression
- **Before major releases** — verify the harness is holding
- **When a promoted rule seems to have stopped working** — diagnose with targeted eval run

## Eval Directory Structure

```
.evals/
  EVAL_INDEX.md          # Index of all eval cases with status
  cases/
    eval-YYYYMMDD-001.md # Individual eval case
    eval-YYYYMMDD-002.md
    ...
```

## Creating an Eval Case

### Input

From harness-updater or manually:
- Pattern-Key of the promoted learning
- The rule that was added to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
- What to test (the assertion)
- Verification method

### Eval Case Format

```markdown
---
id: eval-YYYYMMDD-NNN
pattern-key: [from learning]
source: [LRN-YYYYMMDD-001, ERR-YYYYMMDD-003]
promoted-rule: "[the rule text in CLAUDE.md]"
promoted-to: CLAUDE.md
created: YYYY-MM-DD
last-run: YYYY-MM-DD
last-result: pass | fail | skip
---

## What This Tests

[One sentence: what failure this eval prevents from recurring]

## Precondition

[What must be true for this eval to be runnable]
- File X exists
- Project uses framework Y
- etc.

## Verification Method

[One of: grep-check, command-check, file-check, rule-check]

### grep-check
Search for a pattern that should (or should not) exist:
```
target: src/**/*.ts
pattern: "hardcoded-secret-pattern"
expect: not_found
```

### command-check
Run a command and check the exit code or output:
```
command: npm run typecheck
expect_exit: 0
```

### file-check
Verify a file or section exists:
```
target: CLAUDE.md
section: "## Verification"
expect: exists
```

### rule-check
Verify a rule exists in an instruction file:
```
target: CLAUDE.md
contains: "[the promoted rule text or key phrase]"
expect: found
```

## Expected Result

**Pass:** [What "good" looks like]
**Fail:** [What regression looks like]

## Recovery Action

If this eval fails:
1. [Specific step to diagnose]
```
